subject.title: Feature: Built-in pace-aware rate limiting for autonomous agents

question: Should OpenClaw add core pace-aware provider usage controls for autonomous agents, and should the first step be observability-only or include enforcement?
rationale: Source inspection cannot safely choose the product semantics for provider-specific pace projection, persisted state, new config/defaults, and autonomous throttling behavior.

options.title: Phase observability first
options.body: Capture and expose provider usage or pace context without blocking agent or subagent work until the data model proves reliable.

options.title: Add opt-in enforcement now
options.body: Introduce disabled-by-default pace thresholds that throttle subagents or non-interactive work with explicit tests and operator recovery guidance.

options.title: Design plugin/API hooks first
options.body: Keep core lean by first defining provider and agent hooks that let a plugin own pace policy without hardcoding Anthropic behavior in core.

recommendation.title: Phase observability first
recommendation.body: Capture and expose provider usage or pace context without blocking agent or subagent work until the data model proves reliable.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest history across provider usage, status, gateway usage, and plugin usage hook surfaces.
